summary: Distinct project milestone: the related record covers first turbines in the separate Chang Le wind segment; this record covers the earlier 500-MW PV phase.

A later first-party update adds a METR onboarding and publication-rights arrangement to Anthropic’s earlier announced embedded-evaluation partnership with Accenture; no comparative effectiveness result is reported.

Turbo is a distinct 9 October checkpoint release based on the 20 September Qwen-Image-2.1 base model; it adds a saved 8-step sampling schedule and prefix KV caching. No matched speed/quality gain is established.
Related evidence that frontier-model chain-of-thought monitorability can vary under adversarial conditions; this record concerns a different model and evaluation regime.
Both assess how agents use retrieved memory; MemCalib measures atom-level influence while the related work adds a trust/action gate.
Independent Carnegie Mellon study evaluates hosted TypeSafe JEV 1.13.0 and tests its decision-only interface on LLM judging; it is a distinct research event from TypeSafe’s product announcement.

WikiSkill studies a persistent knowledge layer that supports skill evolution through validation gating; GraphSkillAA studies addressable graph objects, failure attribution, localized edits and rollback. They investigate complementary designs for evolving agent skills, not the same method or a direct replication.

The SkillsBench study evaluates downstream skill utility across model–harness pairings and skill organization; GraphSkillAA evaluates a method for updating skill-graph state. They cover complementary lifecycle stages and do not independently reproduce each other.

WikiSkill studies how a persistent knowledge layer supports skill evolution across benchmarks and models; this paper studies downstream utility of existing skills across configurations, candidate selection and skill-set organization. They address complementary stages of the agent-skill lifecycle, not the same intervention or a direct replication.

Hydra-0 and LAWA both replace raw embodiment-specific action/world interfaces with intermediate representations, but Hydra-0 uses explicit image-plane action flow while LAWA predicts compact latent transition intentions.
Both examine world-model design choices that can reduce downstream predictive/control burden, but Hydra-0 changes action representation while LpWM changes latent-state geometry.
